spec.title: Jump Game

examples.explanation: A jump from index zero can reach index two, then the last index.
The only first jump lands on a zero before the destination.

spec.summary: Determine whether the last array index is reachable by making forward jumps bounded by each visited value.
spec.description: Start at index 0 of an integer array, where each value gives the maximum permitted forward jump from that index and any shorter positive jump is allowed. Return whether at least one sequence of jumps can reach the last index; an array of length one is already at the destination.

approaches.name: Greedy Farthest Reach
approaches.summary: Scan reachable indices while maintaining the farthest index that any processed position can reach, succeeding once that boundary covers the destination and failing if the scan moves beyond it. Time: The time complexity is O(n) because each index is processed at most once. Space: The space complexity is O(1) because only the farthest reachable index is stored.
thinkingSteps: Summarize all useful jump choices by the farthest position reachable so far.
Only indices within that reachable boundary can provide new jumps.
Extend the boundary with each reachable index's maximum landing position.
The destination is reachable exactly when the boundary reaches it before the scan becomes stuck.

bullets: Each value gives a maximum forward jump, not a required jump length.
The question asks whether the last index can be reached at all.
A zero can block progress if no earlier jump can pass it.
